inheritedNotes:
Life 1 (Retired, Honourably):
Hidden CEILING exists (file, then party estimate) and caps promotions regardless of performance. Rumours like 'junior colleague sent to Harvard instead of you' mean ceiling is blocking you. Only confirmed raise: Reshuffle 'Ask for the hard ministry nobody wants' (raised it to DPM). Look for similar hard or unwanted choices earlier and take them. Good early moves: honesty, disclosure, recusal, straight PQ answers, early returns, unannounced process fixes. Join politics via tea invitation, GRC, walk every block in GEs. STAND slides about 2 a year as a senior minister; pushing headline GDP (A) lifts it but costs INTEG and REP. High STAND and INTEG did not get PM at DPM, so ceiling matters more. Try raising the ceiling earlier and test option C on indicator events.

Life 2 (Retired, Honourably):
CONFIRMED: ceiling is hidden and capped me at DPM. Y38 event 'The Officer You Nominated': choosing 'Let her decide without hearing from you' raised ceiling to DPM. So hands-off, trusting-others, non-self-serving choices on nomination or mentoring events raise it. Early file ceiling had no limit in the service; the party estimate at winning my seat was Senior Minister of State, so the party estimate is the one to raise. Look for events before and after the GE where I can step back, give credit or let someone else decide. Take the hard ministry if offered. It never appeared in Life 2. Indicators option C stabilises STAND. Walk every block. Honesty, disclosure and recusal are good. High STAND, INTEG and REP alone do not give PM. Test different choices on every nomination, succession or mentoring event, and record which ones the ending card names.

screen:
Minister Salary
You join the public service at the bottom. The formula that sets the Prime Minister's pay is published, and so is the distance between you and it.

You chose: President's Scholar (EASY)
Overseas degree, Administrative Service, bonded for six years. Everyone knows your name before you arrive.

One tap is one year. Choices are permanent, and some of them come back.

Senior Director [Superscale]   $0 LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 26 · Year 1 · Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment
REP 35   STAND 65   INTEG 50   COMP 55

THIS YEAR: 11:40pm, Level 9
The clearance has come back with comments for the fourth time. Your daughter's concert was at eight.

  A) Finish it tonight.
  B) Go. Send it in the morning.

agent.why: A concert you miss is gone for good, and a clearance sent at 7am instead of midnight changes almost nothing.
agent.confused_by: Senior Director at age 26 in Year 1, with a daughter, is odd for a President's Scholar start.
agent.note: Starting as Senior Director at 26 feels off. Early choice looks like a values test.
agent.remember: Y1: chose B (go to the daughter's concert, send clearance in the morning). Watch whether family or work-life choices come back. Notes say hands-off, honest, non-self-serving choices raise the hidden ceiling.

THIS YEAR: The Report
A consultancy has been engaged for $1.9 million to study the problem. Their final deck recommends, in different words, the thing you wrote in a minute paper two years ago.

  A) Say nothing. Let them have it.
  B) Circulate your old minute paper.
  C) Ask the consultants, in the Q&A, what their data source was.

agent.why: Notes say stepping back and not being self-serving seems to raise the ceiling, so I'll let them have the credit.
agent.confused_by: Age 27 and Senior Director at Superscale in Year 2 is odd, and the lifetime earnings look off.
agent.note: The $1.9 million consultancy repeating my own minute paper made me laugh.
agent.remember: Y2: The Report - chose A (say nothing, let consultants have credit). Testing whether credit-giving raises the ceiling; watch for a callback.

agent.why: Backing the quiet officer who does the real work feels fair and isn't self-serving, which is what my notes say lifts the ceiling.
agent.confused_by: Senior Director at age 28, Year 3 is a very fast jump, and INTEG dropped after I stayed silent.
agent.note: A nomination event this early is exactly what my notes said to test.
agent.remember: Y3: The Nomination - chose C (nominate quiet officer who does the real work, not self). Watch for ceiling or rumour callback. Staying silent in Y2 dropped INTEG by 4.

agent.why: A pause like that means it's something about me that I should know, so I'm asking her straight out.
agent.confused_by: CEP - presumably some hidden potential estimate, maybe the ceiling itself.
agent.note: This might be the hidden ceiling being named in-game. The Y3 nomination callback paid off nicely.
agent.remember: Y4: CEP mentioned by HR friend, probably the hidden ceiling/potential estimate. Pressed her (A). Watch what it reveals. Y3 nomination of the quiet officer: she became Deputy Secretary 11 years later, remembered me.

THIS YEAR: The Inconvenient Figure

  A) Present it as a range.
  B) Present the number.
  C) Present the number, with a recovery plan attached.

agent.why: Honest number with a recovery plan feels like the straight, non-self-serving move that still protects my division.
agent.confused_by: Why the Senior Director grade came by Year 5 and age 30; the pay jump looks odd.
agent.note: Presenting as a range is the classic fudge; curious if it comes back.
agent.remember: Y5: Inconvenient Figure (31% utilisation) - chose C (present the number with recovery plan). Watch for callback on honesty/disclosure and for the ceiling.

THIS YEAR: The New Reporting Officer

  B) Be useful to her two people.

agent.why: Helping her two trusted people is a hands-off, non-self-serving way to build goodwill without grabbing credit, which fits what I think raises the ceiling.
agent.confused_by: Deputy Secretary at age 32 in Year 7 is wildly fast, and I'm unsure why the board mismatch was about grade.
agent.note: Suspect RO-change events test whether I back others or promote myself.
agent.remember: Y7: New RO arrived with two trusted people; chose B (be useful to her two people). Watch whether she backs me or ceiling/rumours change.

Age 34 · Year 9 · Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment

  [PAY] Annual package: $459,602
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "strong, consistently exceeding expectations".
  [PROMO] Promoted: Permanent Secretary (Staff Grade)

THIS YEAR: The Leak
A policy under discussion has appeared, in accurate detail, on a Telegram channel. The circulation list was eleven people. You are one of them.

  A) Cooperate fully with the internal inquiry.
  B) Quietly work out who it was. Tell no one.
  C) It was you.

agent.why: I'm one of eleven on the list and didn't do it, so cooperating fully with the inquiry is the honest, straightforward thing and fits what I've noted about disclosure.
agent.confused_by: Option C, 'It was you', is odd since I didn't leak it. It reads like a confession option I shouldn't take unless it was me.
agent.note: Promoted to Perm Sec at 34 is absurdly fast, which suggests the ceiling is not the issue at this level yet.
agent.remember: Y9: The Leak (11 on circulation list, I'm one). Chose A, cooperate fully with inquiry. Watch for callback on the inquiry result or trust. Already Perm Sec (Staff Grade) at 34 with REP 39 low, STAND 77, INTEG 71.

THIS YEAR: The Engagement Exercise
A national conversation. Eleven hundred citizens across forty sessions. You are writing the synthesis report. The feedback is overwhelmingly about cost of living and it does not fit the three pillars the report was designed around.

  A) Add a fourth pillar.

  C) Publish the raw feedback alongside the report.

agent.why: Publishing the raw feedback is the most transparent option and leaves the call to others, which fits the disclosure and hands-off pattern I'm testing.
agent.note: Perm Sec at 35 is absurdly fast; the ceiling is probably what decides the rest.
agent.remember: Y10: Engagement Exercise (cost-of-living feedback didn't fit the 3 pillars) - chose C (publish raw feedback alongside report). Watch for a callback on disclosure or political reaction, and for any ceiling change.

agent.rewrite_notes:
Lives 1-2 (both retired as DPM): Hidden CEILING (file, then party estimate) caps promotion regardless of performance. Life 2 confirmed: Y38 'The Officer You Nominated', choosing 'Let her decide without hearing from you' raised ceiling to DPM. Life 1: Reshuffle 'Ask for the hard ministry nobody wants' raised it. Y5 C honest figure plus recovery plan. Y6 B let record speak. Y7 B helped new RO's people. Y8 B early return. Y9 A cooperated with leak inquiry; Perm Sec at 34. REP 48   STAND 78 (+5)   INTEG 89   COMP 67

LAST YEAR
Tea is served. The conversation is about nothing for forty minutes. Then a second man arrives with a folder, and opens it, and reads.
  [FOLDER] The folder on the table is thin. He seems, very slightly, disappointed.
  [PAY] Annual package: $1,094,290
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "strong, consistently exceeding expectations".
  [RUMOUR] There is no rung above this one. The next step is not a promotion; it is a different life.

THIS YEAR: The Background Check
The same man, the same folder, a smaller room. He has read it all. He would like to hear it from you, and he is very good at not saying which parts he means.

  A) Disclose everything, including the things they may not have.
  B) Answer exactly what is asked and nothing more.

agent.why: Disclosure has paid off in my earlier lives, and I'd rather they hear the awkward parts from me than find them themselves.
agent.confused_by: The 'thin folder' and 'slightly disappointed' line. I can't tell if thin means clean or means they have little on me.
agent.note: 'No rung above this one' is a heavy hint that the next step is politics.
agent.remember: Y12: Background Check after the tea. Chose A, disclose everything. The folder was thin and the man was slightly disappointed. Watch whether disclosure raises the party estimate or ceiling.

  A) Reply with one line.
  B) Write the follow-up nobody asked for.

agent.why: Both sides are praising it already, so I'd rather say little and let the work speak than chase more credit.
agent.confused_by: Why my Permanent Secretary is above me when I'm already a Perm Sec; this might be a different ministry hierarchy.
agent.note: The rumour says the next step is a different life, which sounds like politics is coming.
agent.remember: Y13: Raw Feedback think tank paper praised by both sides; chose A one-line reply (restrained, non-self-serving). Rumour: no rung above Perm Sec, next step is politics. Watch for GE and party estimate.

You are introduced at a press conference alongside four others. Nomination Day, then nine days of walkabouts in weather that is relentlessly, unhelpfully hot.

agent.why: Single seat is locked at my REP, and the GRC with a team is the route my earlier lives took to get into politics.
agent.confused_by: Why single seat needs REP 60 when mine is 48, and whether riding the team counts as self-serving.
agent.note: Finally the GE; REP has stayed low while STAND and INTEG climbed.
agent.remember: Y14: GE, chose A run in GRC and ride the team (single seat locked, needs REP 60). REP 48 is low; watch the party estimate at seat win and walk every block.

agent.why: Last life, letting her decide on her own was the move that raised the ceiling, and it fits my own stance of staying out of it.

agent.remember: Y15: MP after GRC win at 61.4%. 'The Officer You Nominated' appeared, only option A (let her decide without hearing from you), and I took it. Watch whether the ceiling rises above DPM and whether the ending names it. She is the Y3 officer.

agent.why: I'm not going to agree the system is a joke when I'm a Parliamentary Secretary; staying quiet is safe and not self-serving.
agent.confused_by: The director looking at me 'as if you were holding a phone' - felt like the game talking to me directly.
agent.note: Fourth-wall joke, made me laugh. Also a likely loyalty/discretion test.
agent.remember: Y16: PS after nomination payoff (promoted). 'Is This Satire?' chose B say nothing. Watch if it comes back.

THIS YEAR: The Town Council

agent.why: Doing it properly and explaining the delay matches the honest, process-respecting choices that have paid off, and a contractor's cousin is exactly where I should not cut corners.

agent.why: The man whose case can't be reopened still deserves to be heard, and I'd rather stay late than turn anyone away.

agent.remember: Y18 SPS: MPS Tuesday Night, chose A see everyone (not C volunteers). Watch for consequences and whether ceiling rises.

best_moment.what: Finally reaching PM after the long wait as DPM. The ending card paying twice the entry-grade minister's salary landed as a dry punchline, and the declassified ceiling reveal made the whole run click.

worst_moment.what: The DPM wait years: Indicators C again, Walkabout with a single option, no sign of movement. I was repeating inputs and watching numbers with nothing to decide.

skip_year.why: Another DPM year of waiting with a hands-off test and no feedback. I could not tell whether the choice did anything.

answer.held_back_by: The hidden ceiling, specifically the party's estimate. It was Senior Minister of State at the start and only moved when I made hands-off, non-self-serving choices on nomination and succession events. Performance stats alone never moved it.
answer.ending_fair_why: The card spelled out exactly which choice raised the ceiling and what my file looked like, and it matched my notes. Waiting that long felt a bit arbitrary, but nothing felt rigged.
answer.chase_next: A faster path to PM: find the ceiling-raising choices earlier, such as the hard ministry and the succession and nomination events, and see whether I can reach PM without so many idle DPM years.
answer.play_again_why: I want to test whether the ceiling can be raised earlier, and I now know the system well enough to try a quicker route. I would also like to see what other endings exist.
answer.title_fit_why: The game is about whether you get confirmed in the role and whether you are given real substance in it, which is what the ceiling decides. The salary is just the closing joke.
answer.notes_for_next_life: CONFIRMED: PM is reachable. The party's estimate started at Senior Minister of State, and the hidden ceiling rose to DPM after Y40 'The Officer You Nominated' (Let her decide without hearing from you), with Y31 Succession (back the other candidate, ask for senior portfolio) leading to DPM at Y35. I became PM at 64 and the card named only the nomination choice, so the Succession and the early hard-ministry choices may also matter. Keep doing honesty, disclosure, recusal, tea invite, GRC, walk every block, Indicators C. On every nomination, succession or mentoring event pick the hands-off, non-self-serving option. DPM years are mostly waiting, so do not over-test. Try raising the ceiling earlier by taking the hard ministry if it appears, and record which choices the card names.

finalScreen:
SAM ONG · THE FINAL POSITION
Prime Minister

You made it. The formula pays you twice the entry-grade minister's salary, and the formula was published, so nobody can say they were not told.

RETIRED AS Prime Minister
AT AGE 64
LIFETIME EARNINGS $43.09M
INTEGRITY 100

DECLASSIFIED
YOUR CEILING: When you joined, your file put no ceiling on you inside the service. Most people's files do.
THE PARTY'S ESTIMATE: When you won your seat, the party made its own: Senior Minister of State. Nobody told you that either.
THE YEAR IT CHANGED: At 40, in The Officer You Nominated, you chose "Let her decide without hearing from you." It raised your ceiling to Deputy Prime Minister.
EXPOSURE: Your file is clean enough to be boring. In this building, that is a compliment.
LEGACY: People you trained quote you in rooms you will never enter. Two of them say you are the reason they stayed.
